## One-way and round-trip tickets
Most domestic fares are for round trips, and they cost much more than one-way tickets. In 2025, round-trip fares accounted for 56%1 of fares and the average round trip flight cost was $4931. One-way fares accounted for the other 44%1 and averaged $2831. A round trip therefore costs less than two one-way tickets bought separately at the average price, although the two groups include different routes and different travelers.

Source: Bureau of Transportation Statistics, quarterly and annual air fare releases1762travelstatisticsbureau.com
The 2026 quarters show the same split with higher prices. In the second quarter of 2026 a round trip averaged $5492 and a one-way ticket $3122, and one-way fares accounted for 45%2 of fares. The published shares and prices do not multiply back exactly to the overall average, so they are best read as a rough split. Even so, the round trip of the second quarter of 2026 cost $564 more than the 2025 average round trip, and the one-way ticket $294 more.

## Airfare by state and airport
Where a trip starts matters as much as when it is booked. The average domestic flight cost differs by hundreds of dollars between states, measured as the average fare of tickets starting at each state's airports in the second quarter of 2026. Each airport counts once in its state's average, whatever its size, and every airport is placed in the state where it stands, so Washington's two airports count for Virginia and Cincinnati's for Kentucky. Washington, DC has no airport of its own and no value.
Wyoming had the highest average at $617.148, followed by Idaho at $587.898 and Louisiana at $582.098. Delaware, with one airport, had the lowest at $200.858, and Hawaii was next at $281.758.
